new_entities.name: Testosterone replacement in hypogonadal men
new_entities.description: Exogenous testosterone therapy given to symptomatic men with documented low testosterone.

new_entities.name: Libido recovery
new_entities.description: Improvement in sexual desire or libido in men with hypogonadism.

edges.effect_quant: A 2018 placebo-controlled meta-analysis found testosterone therapy improved sexual desire/libido in hypogonadal men (SMD 0.17, 95% CI 0.01 to 0.34), with somewhat larger class-level effects in a 2017 network meta-analysis.
edges.population: adult men with symptomatic hypogonadism and consistently low morning testosterone
edges.mechanism: Libido is one of the most testosterone-sensitive symptoms in male hypogonadism, so this is one of the cleanest endocrine replacement signals in the entire brief. Restoring testosterone toward the physiologic range appears to improve sexual desire more reliably than it changes mood or broad vitality endpoints.
edges.summary: Testosterone replacement probably improves libido in hypogonadal men, although the average effect is modest rather than dramatic. The literature is fairly consistent that men with documented low testosterone and sexual symptoms are the subgroup most likely to notice a real benefit.
edges.caveats: This is replacement therapy in true hypogonadal states, not evidence that testosterone boosts sex drive in eugonadal men. Benefit size varies by baseline symptom burden, partner context, age, and how strictly low testosterone is confirmed before treatment.

evidence.citation: Corona G et al 2018 J Clin Endocrinol Metab
evidence.notes: The efficacy and adverse events of testosterone replacement therapy in hypogonadal men: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized, placebo-controlled trials.

effect_quant.comparator: testosterone replacement versus placebo for sexual desire/libido
